problem: Transformer-based agents on outdoor VLN (Touchdown) complete fewer than a quarter of routes because they lack explicit mechanisms to align unsynchronised linguistic and visual sequences, and they depend on large-scale pretraining or external object detectors.
motivation: Humans use priority maps to pick out task-relevant cues, and navigation instructions are dense in references to salient urban features (intersections, awnings, cars). Adding depth to transformers did not help (VisualBERT 8l < 4l), so an explicit alignment and localisation mechanism, pretrained cheaply on in-domain data, is proposed instead.
key_idea: A pretrained priority map module first estimates route step count from path traces to plan which instruction spans apply, then sharpens visual features and localises the relevant span, and its output is fused with a transformer encoder's embeddings for action prediction.
insight: Explicit hierarchical alignment matters far more than model depth. Removing trajectory estimation drops dev TC from 33.0 to 7.1, and no pretraining of g_PMTP gives 4.7. Small in-domain pretraining beats generic data: Conceptual Captions at 100% or 150% size gives 19.8 and 23.9 TC against 33.0 with MC-10. Path traces alone do not explain the gain, since VisualBERT(4l) with path traces reaches only 15.0 TC on test.
method: g_PMTP trajectory estimation: a ConvNeXt-Tiny classifies the step count of a route from its path-trace image, pretrained on TR-NY-PIT-central (17,000 Pittsburgh routes, 66 classes). A Gaussian trajectory plan over the instruction samples the span for the current step, concatenated with the previous step's span.

g_PMF feature-level localisation: visual boost filtering (LoG-based unsharp masking with a learned sharpening term λ) is applied to the current panorama view. The result is concatenated with the predicted span and a single-layer LSTM makes a binary span-localisation prediction.
Pretraining on MC-10: g_PMF is pretrained with a multi-objective loss, cross-modal matching plus geolocation prediction, on 8,100 Wikidata landmarks (text, image, coordinates) from 10 US cities.
Cross-modal attention: PM-VLN outputs e_l and e_v' go through a VisualBERT embedding layer and 4 transformer layers (hidden size 256) for self-attention.

Feature-location framework FL_PM: g_CFns fuses the main-model embeddings (VisualBERT 4l or VLN Transformer 8l, with the Zhu et al. inputs) with the PM-VLN outputs, applies dropout, then a maxout-activation classifier predicts Forward/Left/Right/Stop.
Rotation training policy: path traces are trained upright for 20 epochs, then rotated 180° for a second round.

setting.backbone: VisualBERT (4 layers, hidden 256) + PM-VLN module (ConvNeXt-Tiny, LSTM, conv filter); also VLN Transformer (8l) variant; trained from scratch/pretrained on auxiliary tasks
setting.training_data: Touchdown train (6,525 routes) plus auxiliary pretraining on TR-NY-PIT-central (17,000 Pittsburgh path traces) and MC-10 (8,100 landmarks in 10 US cities); base embeddings from BERT-base as in Zhu et al. 2021
setting.observation: Street-view panorama perspective RGB + instruction text + path-trace image
setting.action_space: discrete: Forward / Left / Right / Stop on Touchdown navigation graph
setting.privileged: none (path traces used as additional input, generated from route coordinates)

numbers.extra: Uses path traces as extra input; pretrained on TR-NY-PIT-central and MC-10; no M50 pretraining

numbers_note: Touchdown is not in the canonical list, so it is labelled other:Touchdown. Development results are reported on the dev partition (use 'val'). Metrics are TC/SPD/SED. Ablation numbers are dev only.
results: FL_PM + VisualBERT(4l) reaches 33.4 TC on Touchdown test, roughly doubling standalone transformers (VisualBERT(4l) 11.8; VLN Transformer(8l) 13.1) and beating the transformer-based VLN Transformer + M50 + style (16.2). It does not beat the non-transformer ORAR (29.1 test TC) on the 'highest overall' claim only in the sense of being transformer-based; actually 33.4 exceeds ORAR's 29.1, though ORAR uses different inputs. SPD is worse (23.8) because of early stops.
limitations: Higher SPD (worse) than baselines, since the agent often predicts Stop before finishing routes.
Evaluated only on Touchdown, with training data tuned to its rectangular urban grid, and path traces are an extra input that baselines lack.
Ablations are on the dev set only, and the theoretical section is largely informal.
